summary.headline: Bikaji Q1 FY27 revenue grew ~12.5% (volume +7.7%) despite a 3–4 day Bikaner plant/dispatch shutdown and labour exits; EBITDA margin ~13.5% vs 12.2% QoQ.
summary.overview: Management described Q1 as a story of two halves: April to mid-May was hit by a 3–4 day shutdown after the Chairman's passing and a loss of Bengali labour around the Bengal elections, while the last ~45 days saw strong recovery, with management citing ~20% growth in that period. Value growth of 12.5% was led by Western Snacks (+21.3%) and Ethnic Snacks (+11.4%), with exports the only weak channel (-2.2%). EBITDA margin was ~13.5% against ~12.2% last quarter, and management guided FY27 EBITDA margin to 13–13.5% including PLI, with festive-season ad spend rising. Price hikes are on hold until Diwali.

financial_highlights.value: INR 12.5 Crores of INR 14 Crores other operating income
financial_highlights.change: Full-year PLI ~INR 50 Crores, booked in equal quarterly parts
Stores up from 15 to 28 in one year

segments.name: Western Snacks
segments.commentary: Grew 21.3% in value, with new product launches in the quarter.

segments.name: Ethnic Snacks
segments.commentary: Grew 11.4%; management said snacks overall grew about 20% in the quarter.

segments.name: Sweets
segments.commentary: Grew 4.4%; festive sweets guided to 12–13% growth across Q2+Q3.

segments.name: Papad
segments.commentary: Declined about 6.5% due to monsoon-related disruption to handmade production; about 6% of business.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Only channel with negative growth, -2.2%; freight costs up 2–3x on crude oil and US tariff issues deferred shipments.

segments.name: Geographies
segments.commentary: Core states +11%, focus states +19% (UP ~37%), other states +5.6%.

segments.name: THF (Tasty Hub Foods) retail
segments.commentary: Plans about 10 store openings this year, targeting ~35 stores this year and 50 in 2.5–3 years; targets INR 700 Crores of business from THF.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin target 13–13.5% including PLI, with at least 50 bps YoY improvement; long-term 15% margin aspiration over 3 years, not this year.
FY27 revenue growth target of 15%+ (management later said mid-teens to ~16% per quarter, high-teens as aspiration).
Festive sweets expected to grow 12–13% and gifting 17–18% across Q2+Q3.
Advertising spend for the full year targeted at about 2% of sales, with heavier ad spend in the next two quarters.
PLI benefit of about 150 bps of EBITDA this year, falling to about INR 50 Crores next year; mitigation of 50–75 bps targeted via pricing and gross margin, with 1.5–2 years to restore original margin.
Core-state growth budgeted at 13–15%; focus states (UP) 30%+ in budget.
No further price increase planned for the next 30 days or until Diwali, as prices are signed off with large accounts.
capex_capacity: New ASRS investment not yet live; about 1 lakh sq ft of construction underway in Bikaner adding 1.2–1.3 lakh cartons of storage capacity.
Plan to manufacture core bhujia in two plants this year, reducing single-site dependence on Bikaner.
Nepal JV: both partners investing about INR 15 Crores each; plant expected in 8–9 months, located between Birgunj and Kathmandu.
Bikaji Bakes (bakery): not yet in full production; trials ongoing, production could start in about two quarters, with no large numbers in FY27 plan.
US business expected to grow about 3x in next 2 years; exports about 3–4% of business now, targeted at 5–6% in 3–4 years.
demand_pricing: Two price increases taken over the last 90 days to offset edible oil and pulse inflation (moth dal, chana dal); one MRP increase taken in April.
Management said modern trade, quick commerce and general trade demand plans for the next 3 months are positive.
Quick commerce: management says top brands account for ~50% of category business on those platforms; Q-com is low single-digit % of category.
Private labels from quick commerce platforms (e.g., Swiggy's Noice) seen as early-stage; management says consumers stay with brands.
Management attributes slow category growth over the past two years to single-digit growth, with GST cut from 12% to 5% providing a post-period uptick.
Distributor inventories were depleted by the disruption and restocking will take time.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the April production loss a factor for the top line, given inventory and recovery time?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said dispatches, not production, were shut for 3–4 days; June was the highest delivery month and July continues momentum. Management also said the labour loss meant minimal production until May 18.

qa_highlights.question: What is the reason for slower standalone growth (about 11% last year) versus the earlier expected 15–17%?
qa_highlights.answer: Category growth fell to single digits over the last two years versus double-digit earlier; Q1 and Q2 of last year were weak due to rains, and the GST cut lifted demand thereafter.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 15% margin target achievable this year, given the ad-spend guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Rishabh Jain said 15% is a 3-year target, not for this year; FY27 is targeted at 13–13.5%, with at least 50 bps improvement YoY.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA outlook for THF stores?
qa_highlights.answer: Each store targets INR 6–8 Crores of sales, with about 25%+ core-level EBITDA; THF targets 15–16% of EBITDA in 3–4 years, growing 40–50% a year.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the export decline and when will it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Freight costs rose 2–3x and container availability was constrained, deferring shipments; management said recovery may take a couple of quarters, with US tariff uncertainty also cited.

qa_highlights.question: What is the core-state growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects core-state growth to return to mid-teens from this quarter, with the budget at 13–15%; focus states budgeted at 30%+, with UP at about 37% in Q1.

risks_watch: Edible oil and pulse inflation; price hikes paused until Diwali, so gross margin recovery depends on mix and efficiencies.
Labour concentration in Bikaner for core bhujia; single-site risk is being addressed by decentralisation.
PLI roll-off (~INR 50 Crores) from FY28, a 150 bps EBITDA headwind.
Exports: freight costs and US tariff uncertainty could delay shipments for a couple of quarters.
Heavy ad spend in Q2–Q3 could keep EBITDA margin under pressure despite gross margin gains.
Quick commerce competition and private-label entrants.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on demand recovery and festive pipeline, but more cautious and sometimes evasive on margins, export timing and the reconciliation of the 15% margin aspiration. The Q1 shortfall was attributed to one-off disruptions.

growth.why: Q1 value growth was 12.5% against a 3-4 day shutdown, with management citing ~20% growth over the last 45 days and FY27 revenue guided to mid-teens to ~16%, though Q1 itself fell short of that and the call gives no utilisation figure.
